=== researchPrime v4 (three rounds; ADOPT / VERIFY / INVENT / REJECT; NOT converged — round 3 applied unverified) ===
# researchPrime — Best-in-class evidence for a personal writing skill (v4 — FINAL for the morning; round 3 applied, NOT re-verified)

**Date:** 2026-09-05/06 · **Requested by:** John (overnight) · **Steering seat:** Fable 5.1 · **Evidence seats:** three (tooling A, literature B, craft/workflow C) · **Ledgers:** `ledger-A-tooling.md` (67 claims, 18-tool matrix, fetched 2026-09-05), `ledger-B-literature.md` (45 works, 2022–2026), `ledger-C-craft.md` (73 claims; C-48 carries an appended round-3 correction). Rungs are the seats' own (OBSERVED > CORROBORATED > CLAIMED > UNVERIFIED).

**Verification state (read this first):** three engine rounds ran (Grok panel on v1; Grok panel on v2 merged with an independent ChatGPT-family auditor; Grok panel on v3). Each round's findings were applied to the next version. **Round 3's findings are applied in THIS v4 and have NOT been re-verified** — the three-round budget is spent and the engine's state is NOT CONVERGED (open items are listed in the stamp at the end, not hidden). Treat the F-sections as reviewed twice, the ADOPT/VERIFY/INVENT/REJECT lists as reviewed three times and corrected once more without a fourth look.

**AXIS:** what mechanism makes (1) series-bible consistency checking, (2) flow tracking bible → outline → beats → draft → revise → submit, and (3) voice-preserving dictation intake TRACTABLE for one author across two novel series, a literary short-story collection and an essay collection — and which parts should be ADOPTED from evidenced practice versus INVENTED. A candidate is falsified if a cheaper, proven mechanism already covers the requirement, or if the evidence shows it fails at book/series length.

**Stakes:** medium — reversible; the plan and the North Star build on this.

**Three kinds of statement, kept apart:** LEDGER EVIDENCE (cited [A/B/C-n] with rung); SESSION EVIDENCE (tests run tonight by this run's own seats — real, n = 1, not in a ledger); LOCAL (from INTAKE — John's requirements and corpus facts, not findings of the evidence pass).

---

## Findings, ranked by consequence

### F1 — No audited cross-book, series-scale continuity checker was found; intra-book and outline-scale checking has prior art to adopt.
**Scope of the absence:** ledger A's matrix of 18 tools (commercial AI, classic outlining, analytical, the 2026 continuity-checker micro-market, open-source agentic) plus the human baseline, fetched 2026-09-05; ledger B's 45-work survey. "Not found in this pass", not proof. **What exists:** Sudowrite's continuity is context injection by its own account [A-3, OBSERVED]; NovelCrafter's Codex has no checking layer and its series recipe is a hand-written summary per prior book [A-11, A-12, OBSERVED]; Plottr and Dabble have no AI [A-15, A-20]; Scrivener, Campfire, World Anvil have no checking [A-17–A-19]. **Checkers that exist:** Bunsho (shipped; contradiction flags and plan-time preflight; effectiveness CLAIMED) [A-25]; Marlowe's "inconsistencies review" (mechanism undisclosed, CLAIMED) [A-23, A-24]; the 2026 micro-market, no published precision/recall [A-28, A-67]; open-source LibriScribe and Novel-OS with code-level invariant checks (mechanism OBSERVED, output UNVERIFIED) [A-33, A-34]; research checkers — FactTrack (outline scale), ConWriter (generation-time, up to 12K-word generations), ConStory-Checker (LLM judge with quoted evidence) [B-16, B-17, B-18]. **Length:** the longest consistency-evaluated GENERATION found is ConWriter's 12K words [B-17]; plot-hole DETECTION at length is studied and degrades as narratives lengthen [B-14, OBSERVED]. **Consequence:** adopt the intra-book/outline-scale parts (F2); the series-scale composition is the invention (INVENT-1), and its known risk is that detection degrades with length.

### F2 — The parts of a checker are evidenced (each on its own task); the assembled series-scale recipe is a hypothesis.
(a) Structured external state validated before commit: ConWriter reports 50–87% consistency-error-density reduction on n = 20 LLM-generated stories scored by an LLM judge, as a generation-time wrapper — **direction usable; magnitude single-source, LLM-judged, not measured on a human manuscript** [B-17; A-39]; DOME's −87.61% is its own paper's figure and ConWriter's Table 1 shows DOME sometimes worse than a direct baseline — **direction only** [B-6]. (b) FactTrack's representation — pre-facts/post-facts with validity intervals; contradiction = interval overlap ∧ semantic conflict; retrieval prunes pairs — evaluated at OUTLINE scale and on the ContraDoc document benchmark (single-source F1 figures) [B-18, OBSERVED]. (c) NLI as a high-recall filter (SummaC — a summarisation-inconsistency task) [B-21] and LLM adjudication that must quote spans (ConStory-Checker) [B-16] — evidenced separately; **nobody has run the combined ladder**. (d) LLM extracts, code checks invariants — LibriScribe (dead character / destroyed location) and Novel-OS (dormant thread, absent character, anachronism) are each prior art to copy; **neither has an audited output** [A-33, A-34]. (e) Risks for any primary check: LLM plot-hole detection degrades with length and LLM summarisation/generation inject holes (+50%/+100%, measured on LLM outputs) [B-14]; long context is not state (mid-context recall −30%; NoLiMa 99.3% → 69.7% at 32K) [B-23, CORROBORATED]; "is this consistent?" yes/no asks meet training-induced sycophancy [B-30, CORROBORATED]. Graph-structured control helped plot-driven material and not introspective narrative [B-11] — the Eddy stories would be checked on facts, not interiority. NCP-Bench's 42% / 40–68% figures are interactive-agent measurements — **direction only, wrong task for a manuscript checker** [B-19; A-37].

### F3 — The documented staffed-franchise continuity pattern: a separate person, an entity glossary plus a date-keyed timeline, and (CLAIMED) canonization after each book.
Documented examples, not a ranked population: Dragonsteel — a named continuity editor, an internal wiki, and a 1,100-row Master Cosmere Timeline storing elapsed time as data with the justifying quote, chapter, and on-day/past/future [C-33, A-58, A-59, OBSERVED]; Team Jordan — house glossary plus consolidated notes and dual-channel search [C-37, C-38, OBSERVED]; GRRM — two superfans [C-40, CORROBORATED]; Kowal — birth years not ages; "if it's not in the document, it is not canon" [C-42, OBSERVED]; the bible lists foreshadowing and reader-promises among its contents [C-41, OBSERVED]; a canonization loop after each book — CLAIMED (transcript excerpt; page not fetched) [C-43]. **Counter-models:** Tolkien — no bible, no continuity editor, reconstructed posthumously [C-44]; the trade copy editor — one open Word document and a hand timeline [A-55]; "continuity editor" is not a standard trade title [C-45]; what catches an error in first-person accounts is a person's attention or dual retrieval, never an automated pass [A-62]. For a one-author skill the "separate person" is what is being replaced; what transfers is the artifact shape and the canon rule. Lucasfilm's Story Group queries canon before writing — the pre-write precedent [A-56, CORROBORATED].

### F4 — Voice drift under LLM revision is measured on non-fiction; a production voice gate for fiction is not validated; dictation: restructure over regenerate as a provisional default.
LLM revision moved personal-narrative voice in the same direction across the three models tested (fewer contractions and function words, more lexical diversity and punctuation elaboration; magnitudes single-source, measured on Hippocorpus / oral histories / Reddit — **not fiction, not transferable as thresholds**); an explicit "preserve my voice" prompt reduced but did not redirect the effect [B-32, OBSERVED]. Post-editors rated LLM-drafted text as their own while measurable signature remained (n = 81, vows and apology letters; **direction only**) [B-33, OBSERVED]. The 13-marker battery and authorship-embedding distance are a non-fiction analysis harness with an evaluation triad [B-32, B-37]; **no operating thresholds for fiction exist** — a fiction gate is INVENT. Continuation over instruction and 2–5-exemplar saturation are CLAIMED (aggregator) [B-34]; ~16-exemplar prefix conditioning is a different, abstract-level claim [B-35]. Dictation: gist extraction + macro operations over the speaker's own words (Rambler; diary study) [B-43, B-44, OBSERVED]; practitioner costs — ~40-word dictated sentences, paragraph-level rewrite, net time ≈ zero [C-67, CORROBORATED]; start with notes, not drafting [C-60]; placeholder names + Replace-All [C-63, CLAIMED]. **Provisional default:** restructure his own words rather than regenerate, evaluated by the sit-beside test on his prose. Access to AI story ideas raised individual quality while making stories across USERS more alike [B-27, OBSERVED — a population measurement]; professional writers valued brainstorming/partner use most and called whole-story generation a dead end [B-39, OBSERVED]. **SESSION EVIDENCE (not ledger):** a Gandalf Grok refuter's counter-experiment tonight (n = 1; same family as the panel) — a "sacred-hedged" rewrite of one of John's stories kept every mechanical counter inside the original band while violating the profile's core rule; it motivates a hypothesis to TEST (semantic markers such as hedging of spiritual events), not a requirement.

### F5 — Three framework layers, not four rivals; kishōtenketsu is a withholding discipline, not "conflict-free"; the two structures can coexist in one work; this blend is an invented composition.
Savage's Four-Part Pacing is publicly undocumented — his site names the class; the only public account is unattributed 2019 conference notes, so its content is CLAIMED [C-1, C-3, C-4]. **LOCAL:** John's July-2025 lecture notes (BrightHeart/Four Part Pacing.docx) are the authoritative source and were not read by this pass. Two distinctive Savage rules surface: a Q1 hook that is NOT the main conflict (not in Weiland) and a final obstacle that is a belief that must crack (coincides with Weiland's Lie) [C-5, C-13]. Act-level template (Savage / Wells / Save the Cat), arc-level Lie/Truth/Want/Need (Weiland), scene-level Scene/Sequel + MRU (Swain) are described separately in the ledger [C-9–C-15]; Story Grid's commandments recur fractally across ITS scales [C-11] — an analogy, not proof that one vocabulary serves Savage + Weiland + Swain. Kishōtenketsu: Chinese origin [C-16]; *ten* is a re-framing, not a twist [C-22]; "plot without conflict" is a 2012 Tumblr artifact disputed by practitioners and called orientalist [C-20, C-21, C-30]; documented cases show Western structure and kishōtenketsu true of one work at once (Miyazaki) [C-23, C-28]. Where a blend must choose per book — the promise/genre contract at the *ten*; closure at the *ketsu* (open endings permitted with a stated US-market risk "worth taking" [C-29]); whether conflict is required at all — is THIS REPORT's decision procedure (framework map), not a published method. **The blend and its per-book choices are an INVENTED composition informed by the evidenced layers.** Korean *giseungjeongyeol* is the closest documented cousin of a revelation-over-conflict shape [C-26]; mapping it onto the Eddy is LOCAL (ledger C did not read John's corpus).

### F6 — Trilogy from one manuscript: the Sanderson model with a duology kill-gate; name the age category before the length.
Book 1 standalone with a real ending, deeper outlines for 2–3 afterwards (Sanderson), not "cut the mega-arc in three" (Wells) [C-52, OBSERVED]; cut shortly after a significant triumph [C-50]; each book carries its own Normal World, inciting incident, climax, resolution, mini-arc and escalated stakes [C-51, C-55]; if book 2 has no story of its own, write a duology [C-56, CORROBORATED]. **Length — SINGLE-SOURCE, DIRECTION ONLY, held in VERIFY:** the cited 2026 agent-facing page as re-read by two round-2/3 seats [C-48, OBSERVED single vendor page; the ledger row's original CORROBORATED figures were a mash and are corrected by an appended note]: MG target 40–60k (contemporary 40–50k; fantasy/adventure to ~60k); YA target 60–80k (fantasy ~80k or slightly above; over 90k a red flag that needs a reason); adult fantasy a separate 90–120k band. HP1 is reported at 76,944 words / 17 chapters (fan-count sources, no publisher primary) [C-46, CORROBORATED]; "below the commercial sweet spot" is one 2016 essay [C-47, CLAIMED]. **LOCAL:** "Harry Potter 1 age group" is John's framing from INTAKE; on that one page an HP1-shaped 75–80k book sits in YA-fantasy territory, not core MG — **the category decision is his, and it precedes any length target**. Write the series bible at the moment book 1 is done, including the promises book 1 made [C-41].

### F7 — The pipeline is severed at both ends; the "one corpus, four forms" absence is CLAIMED.
**Scope:** not found across ledger A's 18 surveyed tools (commercial AI, classic outlining, analytical, micro-market, open-source; fetched 2026-09-05) — no tool tracks a work bible → outline → beats → draft → revise → submit; craft tools stop at draft, Duotrope / Chill Subs / Submittable begin at submission, writers bridge with Kanban boards [A-45, C-68, CORROBORATED]. Kishōtenketsu appears in none of those 18 tools' templates [A-47, OBSERVED absence, same scope]. "Nothing treats novels + stories + essays as one authorial corpus" is CLAIMED [A-48]. Collection ordering consensus: best first, second-best last, contrast 1 vs 2, tent poles, a hinge story mid-book [C-70, CORROBORATED]; essay collection: the first essay teaches the reader how to read the book [C-72, C-73, CLAIMED].

---

## Recommendation — adopt / verify / invent / reject (v4)

**ADOPT (each individually evidenced on a named task; cite when building):**
1. Ahlstrom's timeline shape — a date-keyed timeline storing elapsed time as data, every fact with its receipt (quote, chapter, on-day/past/future) [A-58, A-59 OBSERVED]. 1b. Kowal's rules — birth years not ages; canon = what is in the document [C-42 OBSERVED]. 1c. Foreshadowing and reader-promises as bible contents [C-41 OBSERVED]. 1d. An entity-keyed glossary beside the timeline (Dragonsteel, Team Jordan) [C-33, C-37 OBSERVED].
2. Validate-before-commit as a DIRECTION: immutable bible vs evolving state; nothing enters the bible unchecked [B-17 direction; B-6 direction].
3. FactTrack's fact representation: pre/post-facts with validity intervals; contradiction = interval overlap ∧ semantic conflict; retrieval-pruned candidate pairs [B-18, outline-scale evidence].
4. NLI as a high-recall candidate filter — evidenced on summarisation inconsistency, to be re-validated on fiction [B-21]; LLM adjudication that must quote spans and cite ids [B-16] — as separate components.
5. "LLM extracts, code checks" — copy LibriScribe's and Novel-OS's mechanisms as prior art; no audited output exists for either [A-33, A-34].
6. Querying canon BEFORE writing — the Lucasfilm Story Group practice [A-56 CORROBORATED]. (River's summary-only limit [A-26] and Bunsho's preflight [A-25 CLAIMED] are context, not the basis.)
7. Setup → payoff as a first-class bible relation (the idea, not a series-scale checker) [B-20 OBSERVED; C-41 OBSERVED].
8. The IDEA of cheap stylometric measurement plus an authorship-distance check as an evaluation harness (validated on non-fiction only) [B-32, B-33, B-37]; gist-preserving dictation over the author's own words [B-43, B-44 OBSERVED].
9. Sanderson debut model + duology kill-gate + cut-after-a-triumph for the Bright-Heart split, with the age category named first [C-52, C-56, C-50]. (Length bands are NOT adopted — see VERIFY.)
10. Kishōtenketsu read as a withholding discipline [C-18] and the documented fact that it can coexist with Western structure in one work [C-23, C-28]. (The three-layer composition and the per-book pick-a-side procedure are NOT adopted — see INVENT.)

**VERIFY before it can be adopted:** the canonization loop after each book (fetch Writing Excuses 12.30) [C-43 CLAIMED]; exemplar counts and continuation-over-instruction (re-verify [B-34] against primaries); the MG/YA length bands [C-48 — one vendor page, re-read twice; needs a second 2026 agent source before any target is set].

**INVENT (hypotheses to prove on John's material; scope of each "not found" stated):**
- The composed, tiered check ladder (deterministic lint → retrieval → NLI filter → quoted adjudication → local re-read) over a SERIES bible — parts evidenced, composition unrun by anyone [B design implications; A-35]; known risk: detection degrades with length [B-14].
- Cross-book, cross-trilogy thread dependency checking over a planted/paid ledger with `depends_on` (nearest work narrow and 2026: NCP-Bench commitments, CFPG setup→payoff) [B-19, B-20; B open 4].
- The three-layer framework composition (act template / arc Lie-Truth / scene Scene-Sequel) with one beat vocabulary, and the per-book pick-a-side procedure for the kishōtenketsu blend (promise contract at the *ten*; closure at the *ketsu*; whether conflict is required) — this report's own composition; no named published hybrid method in scope [C-9–C-15, C-23, C-28, C-29 as inputs].
- A per-author, per-project fiction voice lint with operating thresholds, bidirectional (too conventional / too florid) — a design hypothesis; ledger B did not search "bidirectional profile linting" (not searched, not "no prior art"). Candidate semantic markers come from SESSION EVIDENCE (F4) and are to be tested.
- One corpus, four forms, one status record — a LOCAL requirement (the Steward), not an evidence finding [A-48 CLAIMED for the market absence]. Provenance tags ([AUTHOR]/[DEVELOPED]/[SUGGESTED]) are a local design choice already practised in the corpus's own collection-writer.

**REJECT (evidence-based, with its strength):**
- Full-manuscript LLM consistency passes as the DEFAULT primary check — provisional, risk-based: the evidence is on LLM outputs [B-14] and long-context recall [B-23]; no manuscript-checker study exists either way. - "Is this consistent / good?" yes-no asks as a judgement surface [B-26, B-28, B-30]. - Whole-story or whole-chapter generation as the working mode [B-39: the writers themselves called it a dead end]. - "Kishōtenketsu = no conflict" encoded as fact [C-20, C-21].
- NOT rejected (corrected in v4): partner-style plot brainstorming — the cited writers valued it most [B-39]; homogenisation across users [B-27] is carried as a measured multi-user RISK, not a ban.
- (LOCAL constraint, not evidence: no fifth prose-only orchestrator — the corpus already holds four; see INTAKE.)

**Representative baselines (features, not rankings):** NovelCrafter Codex + Progressions — typed entries, time-scoped one-directional facts [A-7, A-9]; Ahlstrom's Master Timeline — elapsed time as data, receipts, 1,100 rows [A-58]; FactTrack — interval facts, retrieval-pruned NLI, outline scale [B-18]; Sudowrite Match My Style — prose-sample voice matching, typed input only [A-5]; Bunsho — plan-time preflight, CLAIMED [A-25].

**Foresight receipt (Oranges):** dropped branch — fine-tuning a voice model on his prose (Weaver / Muse-style [B-8, A-6]) — dropped on COST and LOCK-IN grounds (months of work, a frozen voice, no training path on his subscription-seat host), not on a measured performance comparison; whether exemplars capture "most of the gain" is unmeasured (exemplar figures CLAIMED [B-34]). Reordered — dictation-to-prose behind the ledger/check slice: regeneration is where voice drift is measured [B-32, B-43], so the first dictation product is capture + classify + check, not draft.

=== PLAN PREVIEW (the steering seat's proposed slices, cuts, Rabbit-Catcher verdicts — a preview to be forged, not the plan) ===
# Plan preview — the writing skill (for John's morning review, 2026-09-06)

**What this effort is for:** one foundry skill that keeps each writing project's bible checkable, knows where he is, checks dictated ideas against the plot before they break it, and writes in his own voice — so *Artificial Magi* Book 1, a clean *Bright-Heart* Book 1 (+ trilogy plan), and the *Sing for the Dead* stories get out.

**Where tonight's run stopped:** Crucible Stage 0 halted at its first human gate. Nothing is locked, nothing is built. Three decisions are yours; I will ask them **one at a time** in chat, each with a recommendation. They are listed here only so you can see the whole shape.

## The three decisions (in order)

1. **Salvage or rewrite the four existing project skill-sets?** — Recommendation: **salvage the prose, rewrite the orchestration.** The forms (Four-Part, Three-River, Eddy, Prosecution), the voices (magi / brightheart / sing), the editorial judgement and the session protocol are good text and become the packs and profiles; the orchestration (four hand-copied cascade-writers, three hand-updated status files) is replaced by the engine. Cost: the four folders' `.claude/skills` become consumers of the canonical skill (Anchor-style), not sources.
2. **Lock the North Star** (`crucible/NORTH-STAR-CANDIDATE.md`, printed in full at the ask). — Recommendation: **lock**. The one thing that gets worse: the bible's source of truth becomes markdown the engine can check; Word files are rendered from it (Grok refuted the ledger on the current docx-first state; ChatGPT grounded it conditional on exactly this acceptance).
3. **The name.** — Recommendation in the morning message (Jumper's proposal + the steering seat's shortlist: Chekhov / Le Guin / Munro / Cather / Welty).

=== JUMPER (Heavy, single candidate; Gate 3 REJECTED — the mechanism is a hypothesis, the corrections in the kill log are adopted) ===
DELIVERABLE:
MECHANISM: THE BOAT SHEET. One law: every dictated entry is born with a qualifier and is usable at once at that rung; it becomes binding only at the next mount-time plotting session, off the dictation path. Hot path = leadsman's call. Settlement = survey. Nothing model-shaped runs while he talks.

REPRESENTATION (Node + markdown; no DB, no embeddings)
1. Chart = the bible, made checkable by fenced YAML beside the prose it annotates. Prose still saying six is non-canonical by rule (the struck-through symbol); src/at is the margin log the bible never had.
  - id: series.book_count  q: assert  v: 7  t: [B1,B7]  lock: locked  src: bible.md#L42  at: 2026-09-05
  - id: thread.marshal-title  q: assert  plant: B3.12  due: [B3.12,B5]  pay: null | release: 'unfired by design'
  - alias: {Marshal: {id: char.tarn, t: [B3.04,B7]}}
Qualifiers cut to four: propose | assert | ask | release. Lock rungs cut to three: candidate | relied | locked; relied is derived at settlement from draft references, never asserted at capture. Facts, threads, aliases and the skill's own name share this one tuple shape.
2. Sailing Directions = one tenets.md per project. Each prose tenet ('lyn undoes hate') carries a stored witness: a three-line sketch of the scene that would violate it. Judged only at settlement by a verify seat: nearer the witness than not?
3. Boat sheet = sheets/<iso-ts>.jsonl, append-only, one line per idea: {ts, lane, raw, q, hits, verdict: ok|unknown|CONTRADICTS|pencil, dismissed}. This IS the memory. Brief, stage, status line and Ecgberht's Face line are replayed from sheets + chart; delete and regenerate: identical, exercised daily by ordinary use.

HOT PATH (per idea, seat-free, under 1 s): alias-trie hit -> interval overlap against LOCKED facts only -> value conflict. Three-valued: no hit = UNKNOWN, never safe; an unknown proper noun is a forward declaration (q:propose, debt owed at settlement). Interrupt ONLY when the idea contradicts a locked fact it is actively building on: shoaling under the keel. Everything else, true errors included, pencils to the sheet.

SETTLEMENT ('twain settle', runs at next mount, so abrupt endings cost nothing): ratify forward declarations; derive relied; Grok/ChatGPT verify candidates being locked; judge tenets against witnesses; Claude renders pencilled ideas in the project's voice; emit decision packages for forks.

VOICE GUARD (zero per-idea cost): raw dictation is germline by provenance stamp (prov: dictated). Renders are born only at settlement (prov: render) and pass a two-hypothesis gate over five counts per 100 words: em-dash, hyphen-compound, semicolon-list, sentence-length variance, sacred-noun-as-plain-fact. Accepted if nearer the project profile (voice/eddy.json, ya.json, lit-fantasy.json) than the model-prose centroid. Away from both = authorial drift, accepted and logged. Toward the model = normalisation, rejected with the diff shown. Baseline seeded only from dictated or hand-written prose dated before the first render; hand-edited renders stay somatic.

PREVENTION FIRST: 'twain brief <project>' emits the passage plan before dictation, under 200 words: who is alive, what is locked in this scope, threads due in this book, forks open. Use-before-plant, due-by-scope and authored release get their first register here, in reader order.

STAGE: replayed from gate events on the sheet (gate.pass, gate.regress), never max-of-gates, so a bible change can send a book back to outline.

WHAT ECGBERHT SEES ('twain status --line', one derived line, no copy held), e.g.:
twain | fantasy: draft B3.12 | locked 214 | forks 1 | threads due 3 | pending 2 | dismissals/session 0.4
Dismissals/session is the vital sign; above 3 it trips a schema re-derivation task. This tool dies of fatigue, not of misses.

INAUGURAL ACT (stage the known wreck): converting the fantasy bible yields two q:propose values for series.book_count. Decision package, under 200 words:
'FORK series.book_count. bible.md#<a>: six. bible.md#<b>: seven. A) six: seven-book matter folds into book 6; every thread due in B7 falls overdue at B6 (count shown). B) seven: six-book threads keep their dues; one book's outline is owed. Cut: nothing else changes; both stay propose until you pick. Reply A or B.'

DEBTS OWED BEFORE CREDIT (crosslines): (1) one dictated paragraph through the real channel, fingerprinted, before the eddy lane trusts the gate; (2) one timing run at seven-book volume (~5,000 facts, ~800 threads) before 'seconds' is claimed; (3) proven silence on the known-consistent 80% of the current bible before credit for catching 6/7.

CUT LEDGER: four qualifiers, not INT1's dozen; three lock rungs; one tenets file, no per-lane machinery; no retrieval, no embeddings, no database; no seat on the hot path; a five-count voice gate, not a model; one JSONL per session is the whole memory.

NAME (q:propose): twain. Samuel Clemens took his pen name from the leadsman's call 'mark twain': two fathoms, safe water. His craft principle in Life on the Mississippi is this mechanism untranslated: learn the river by heart; it changes every night; take the cheap sounding before every doubtful reach; the pilots' association's shared river notices kept every memorised chart corrected daily. Collision: TWAIN is the 1992 scanner-driver standard; npm scan owed; branch 'clemens' held open. Chekhov and Tolkien each name half (threads, bible) and are released with reason; Twain names the severance. Ratified at first settlement: the first decision package the skill runs.

SYMMETRICAL RESOLUTION:
The Boat Sheet: one law, two artefacts, one projection. LAW: every dictated entry is born with a qualifier (propose | assert | ask | release) and is usable immediately at that rung; it becomes binding (locked) only at the next mount-time settlement, off the dictation path, where all verify seats, tenet judgments, voice gates and renders live. The hot path is a leadsman's call: alias-trie hit, interval overlap against locked typed facts only, value conflict, three-valued on unknowns, and it interrupts solely when the idea contradicts a locked fact it is actively building on. TWO ARTEFACTS: the chart (fenced YAML tuples annotating the bible in place: id, q, v, interval, lock rung, src, at; threads are the same tuple with plant/due/pay-or-release; aliases are interval-scoped tuples) and the Sailing Directions (one tenets.md whose prose tenets each carry a stored violating-scene witness). ONE PROJECTION: the append-only per-session JSONL sheet plus the chart IS the memory; the pre-dictation brief, stage, status line and Ecgberht's Face line are regenerated from it, so 'no second copy' is structural and delete-regenerate-identical runs daily as a side effect of use. Voice costs nothing per idea because raw dictation is germline by provenance stamp; renders are born only at settlement and pass a two-hypothesis punctuation gate (toward the model centroid = normalisation, rejected; away from both = drift, accepted), with the baseline seeded only from pre-render dated author prose. Reliance is derived at settlement from draft references, so locks happen without the author asserting them and without a seat on the drafting path. Dismissals per session is a typed vital sign with a tripwire. The name is itself a q:propose tuple, collision-checked and ratified at first settlement. Full instantiation is in the deliverable.

GATE-3 KILL (Grok):
BLOCKER: the hydrographic transfer leaves the sounder behind, so the hot path's value-conflict is a hallucinated capability. In the foreign domain a sounding is born typed (a depth). Dictation is born as ASR/prose. The advertised hot path is alias-trie hit -> interval overlap against LOCKED facts only -> value conflict, with nothing model-shaped while he talks. No bounded parse, capture grammar, per-kind extractor, or worked utterance-to-verdict trace is instantiated. Without that sensor, a scene such as 'Tarn is already the Marshal in book two' cannot produce a typed (id, v, t) against which interval overlap and value conflict run. The remaining forks all break the contract: a model on the hot path violates d-3 and the one law; an unstated constrained verbal protocol is not a mechanism; keyword presence alone is not FactTrack-style semantic conflict. Treating capture as already-typed is the Dirac asymmetry.

Requirement (c) fails for threads. 'Breaks a thread planted earlier or needed later' is an absence (unpaid-due, use-before-plant), not a value conflict on an overlapping locked tuple. The hot path as written cannot see it. The brief is prevention in reader order; settlement is next mount. Neither tells him in seconds during the idea. That is exactly the 42% unpaid-commitment failure the problem cited.

Contradiction 1 is only half-dissolved. Relied is derived at settlement from draft references, but the hot path ignores everything not locked. Relied therefore does not constrain the next idea, so a-2's 'never tentative' is unmet unless verify-to-lock always finishes at mount before talk — assumed, not specified, and contradicted by 'interrupt only when the idea contradicts a locked fact it is actively building on.' The mapping's own 'mariners avoid a PA/Rep danger immediately' is dropped: ECDIS alarms on preliminary features; this checker does not.

Deliverable test (0028 RC-1): the problem asked for one mechanism plus a concrete bible/thread representation, what the Steward sees, and one writer-name — not a shipped engine. Those artifacts are present (YAML tuples, JSONL sheet, `twain status --line`, the <200-word 6/7 fork package, name twain/Clemens with TWAIN/npm collision). RC-1 does not fail for 'being a mechanism.' It fails because the live path that must satisfy (c) is not instantiated as an artifact, only as a slogan.

Secondary gaps: qualifier birth has no assignment rule on free speech (who sets propose|assert|ask|release); unknown proper-noun forward declarations need a seat-free proper-noun detector, and ASR casing will not provide one ('no hit = UNKNOWN' on tokens is fatigue); no-GUI channel for non-interrupt verdicts, so 'tell him in seconds' collapses to silent pencil except for rare shoaling; voice gate's fifth count (sacred-noun-as-plain-fact) is semantic, not a punctuation statistic, and the model-prose centroid corpus is unspecified; symmetry rhetoric claims one tuple shape for tenets and aliases, but tenets.md is prose+witness and aliases are a nested map; stage is a log schema (gate.pass/regress) with no emitter, so (b) has no writer; live-dictation intake (tail, stdin, steward commission) is unnamed.

What is sound and should be kept if the sounder is instantiated: two-artefact store (chart vs Sailing Directions/witnesses); mount-time settlement so abrupt ends are the designed case; release-with-reason; struck-through + src/at for annotate-never-migrate; Steward line as a projection (no second copy); name as a q:propose tuple ratified by the first decision package; the three named debts (fingerprint, 5k-fact timing, silence-before-credit). Those debts do not buy the missing sounder.

Reject. To pass: instantiate the sounder (one bounded parse or per-predicate extractor) with a single raw dictated sentence traced to hits/verdict in <1s; put unpaid-due and use-before-plant on that same path or explicitly demote (c) to brief+settlement; either include relied in the check set or drop the a-2 claim.

## Success criteria
- Bright-Heart's own bible passes the deterministic lint with zero self-contradictions (six-vs-seven books, chapter-length rule, doctrine tag) BEFORE any new outline is produced — verified on the ledger report John opens on his screen.
- A dictated idea receives a Consistent / Consistent-with-adjustments (ripple list) / Inconsistent (alternatives) verdict that cites ledger entry ids and quoted lines, in under 60 seconds on his machine, with no cross-family seat.
- Every recorded drift in the two series' histories (six-vs-seven books; 14 chapters at 6.5–8k words vs the 3.5–4.5k rule; the kishōtenketsu leak into Appendix A; el/Remi/Elra, Raggi/Corvo, Daguan/Durgan naming; Jess's relationship; 2,500 vs 3,500-word chapters; Anya 13 vs Jess 11) is caught by the T0 lint or the T1 judge when replayed as a fixture — the regression corpus ships with the skill.
- "Where am I / what next" for each project comes from ONE status record that the Steward's Strip also reads; the skill and the Steward never disagree.
- Generated or restructured prose carries [AUTHOR]/[DEVELOPED]/[SUGGESTED] provenance into the rendered docx, and the voice GUARD — mechanical counts PLUS semantic markers (hedging of spiritual events with "as if"/"seemed", stance, sentence-length variance) PLUS the sit-beside model test — separates "Sing for the Dead" from two deliberately normalised rewrites of it: one mechanically flattened, one "sacred-hedged" (session evidence, 2026-09-05: a Gandalf refuter's n=1 experiment showed such a rewrite passes every mechanical counter — a hypothesis this criterion tests, not a settled fact).
- The Eddy form pack (Concerto + Symphony) can be handed to another writer with no sing-voice rule inside it.
- The cross-family adversarial pass (Grok / ChatGPT seats from Anchor prefs) fires only at lock events — book outline lock, bible version bump, "send to editor" — or on request; never per idea.
- The first real job (Bright-Heart decision record + Book-1 cleanliness pass, or the Artificial Magi Spine v4 consistency pass) leaves a journal entry BEFORE any further build wave (usage before waves).
- THE 30-SECOND TEST on John's screen: from the session-start surface he can name project, cascade position, next action and what is waiting on him within 30 seconds, and it is no more burdensome than "Work on X" is today.

Chekhov is built as one engine in six phases, mechanism before prose. Phase 0 grounds text-only git project roots and the regression corpus inside the skill. Phase 1 is the proof slice: the ledger as fenced YAML inside the bible markdown, the T0 deterministic lint with its report, the bounded typed intake traced end to end in this plan (one raw dictated sentence to a cited verdict, absences included), the T1 evidence-table judge with machine-verified cites, and the five-field STATUS.json pushed through Ecgberht's own single-writer heartbeat, proven on Bright-Heart's own bible with a frozen pre-decision snapshot as fixture #1; no docx exists in this phase. Phase 2 is usage, not code: the Bright-Heart decision record, the Book-1 cleanliness pass, criterion 1 on John's screen, the 30-second test and the journal entry that unblocks everything after; the build waits for John. Phase 3 salvages the four skill-sets as form packs and private voice profiles. Phase 4 runs the criterion-5 voice experiment under a pre-registered decision rule before any prose is generated, then provenance as bracket tags in the rendered docx, the render itself, and restructure-only dictation. Phase 5 adds lock-event cross-family passes. This revision cuts sixteen pass-1 elements and moves two, each named in the round-2 resolutions at the end. Every deferral is named in its phase.

## Phase 1 — Phase 0 - Ground: project roots, regression corpus

Serves criteria 3 and 8 and closes the stale-ledger and extraction-cost gates before any engine code exists; nothing in later phases may depend on a Temp scratchpad, a git hook, a zip, or a fifth SKILL.md.

**Near-term specifics:**
- Stable git-tracked project roots for TEXT only, one per project (Artificial Magi, Bright-Heart, Sing for the Dead, Essays), path fixed in Stage 2; the 5.3 GB of mp4 and the audio course stay outside git; the two zips are archived read-only with a checksum recorded.
- Each docx is migrated to markdown only in the phase that needs it (Bright-Heart bible, cascade summary, CLAUDE.md, Book-1 Outline v2 and the 167k manuscript in Phase 2; AM Bible v0.6, Spine v4, Outline v2 in Phase 2; the collection bible in Phase 4; the Freedom of Speech draft in Phase 3's tail); the T0 coverage section lists any docx in a project root with no *_source.md beside it, so nothing unchecked is silent and no hand-kept debt file exists.
- The skill folder <path> Foundry\skills\chekhov is created by the build with the foundry shape: SKILL.md, ELEGANCE block, HUMAN.md, journal/ (NNNN entries plus runs/), test/; the regression corpus lives in test/fixtures inside the skill, never in project data.
- One record format for verdicts and fixtures so a real verdict becomes a regression case with one command (fixture promote); every fixture carries kind real-replay or reconstructed plus its source file, and the criterion-3 report counts the two kinds separately; the criterion-to-fixture mapping lives in the Stage-2 plan's per-wave acceptance criteria, which Foreman already requires.
- Privacy scaffold: confirm the foundry remote is private before the first push (otherwise fixtures are de-identified reconstructions and labelled so); .gitignore for profiles and calibration passages; a skill test that fails if any file under the pack folder contains the calibration-passage marker; fixtures carry minimal excerpts; no git hook of any kind.
- Extraction runs only on an explicit chekhov commit (no git hooks).
- The four project-local .claude/skills sets (AM, BH, Short Stories, Essays) are frozen as read-only cited text; packs and profiles in Phase 3 are new files citing them by section; no orchestration is copied forward.

**Deferred (explicitly):**
- Migrating the Political Shorts lecture library and the Hubert drafts (non-goals); Hubert is read once in Phase 4 only to be excluded or down-weighted from the voice baseline.
- Poetry and Political Shorts project roots are not created in v1; they arrive with their v2 packs.

## Phase 2 — Phase 1 - The proof: ledger, T0 lint, typed intake traced end to end, T1 judge, status record, brief

Serves criteria 1, 2, 3, 4 and 9 and is the fifth-copy gate itself: the ledger, T0/T1 and the status record are the FIRST slice, proven on Bright-Heart's own bible with the six-vs-seven contradiction as fixture #1 (Gandalf d-5; research F2 parts; Jumper's kept artefacts with the sounder instantiated).

**Near-term specifics:**
- The ledger IS the bible markdown: fenced YAML tuples sit beside the prose they annotate (annotate, never migrate); prose that still says six is non-canonical by rule once a decision supersedes it; ledger.json is a rebuilt index every run and is never hand-edited.
- Core tuple fixed to five fields: id, value, interval, lock, receipt; Phase 1 hard-codes the story-time coordinate (book.chapter) for AM and BH, and Phase 3 moves the coordinate into the packs; lock rungs in v1 are candidate and locked only.
- Kinds on the one tuple shape: fact; thread (plant, due, pay, release-with-reason); alias (interval-scoped, storing phonetic and ASR variants such as Elra/Ella); decision (rung provisional or locked, allow_terms whitelist, cost_of_change COMPUTED as the depends_on ripple count); structural-record entry. depends_on edges have three named producers and no other: the extraction call at commit (an entity named inside a fact's receipt span gives an edge to that entity's entries), the decision entry's own governs list (written by John at the ask), and thread entries (the plant and pay scenes give edges to the facts in those scenes); cost_of_change is the size of that closure and is never hand-entered.
- Ids are stable slugs (char.elra, series.book_count, thread.marshal-title); renames become alias entries, never id changes; receipts store the quoted span, heading path, line hint and date, re-anchored by fuzzy match; ages are stored as birth years (Kowal); facts are indexed by entity so interval overlap is per entity.
- chekhov lint (T0, pure, under 2 s) computes: contradictions (interval overlap and value conflict on one id); thread absences (unpaid-due at scope end, use-before-plant) on READER order from the structural record, with written_order and reader_order stored in the series decision record and a fixture proving Bright-Heart's 1,3,2,6,4,5(,7) cascade does not false-flag; a prose pass on the markdown itself for the named ids (book-count numerals and number-words, chapter-length numerals, doctrine terms in headings) independent of extraction; chapter word counts from the manuscript; receipt-drift as its own class; a coverage list of untagged numerals, ordinals, dates and capitalised proper nouns with a threshold John sets.
- The doctrine lint reads the bible, its appendices, outlines and beat sheets in full (prose included — the recorded Appendix A leak sat in the appendix's prose, not in its headings) plus the structural record; it never reads manuscript narrative prose, so a character may say 'conflict' without a flag; initial term lists per doctrine with ordinary-English collisions whitelisted; allow_terms from the decision record permits a Western layer in Bright-Heart; precision and recall measured with the Appendix A prose as the positive fixture and the current post-repudiation AM bible as the negative, figures journaled.
- The refuse-to-outline gate is a T0 rule on the decision record and nothing wider: doctrine tag present, book count single-valued, chapter rule single-valued (the three the locked churn gate names); the refusal prints the missing entries as Speaking-Law asks with a recommendation each, so refusal is also the intake form; the age category is a decision-record ask that precedes any length target but never blocks outlining.
- The verification surface is ONE regenerated LEDGER-REPORT.md with five sections (contradictions / superseded / untagged / receipt-drift / threads due) that the command opens on screen; criterion 1 reads zero contradictions AND the three named ids T0-verified on prose; the untagged count is informational.
- Superseded-span rule, one sentence: a prose span annotated superseded_by <decision id> is excluded from the contradiction count and listed under the report's superseded heading, while any un-annotated span carrying a conflicting value counts — so the live Bright-Heart bible in its project root (annotated after the decision) reads zero for criterion 1, and test/fixtures/brightheart-pre-decision/ (a frozen copy of the migrated markdown taken at the first chekhov commit, before any decision entry exists, named as distinct from the live bible) still reports the six-vs-seven contradiction for criterion 3; the two artifacts are different files and both ship.
- chekhov idea takes pasted text or an inbox file drop and makes ONE bounded typed-extraction call (Jumper's missing sounder) whose output is a fixed schema, never free text: kind (idea / decision / prose / question), scope, claims as (entity, predicate, value, at), unknown_nouns and unknown_predicates; a predicate must be one the pack declares with its cardinality (single-valued: title, alive, location, age, birth_year; multi-valued: knows, has_item, relation) or it is returned as unknown and asked, never invented; unknown proper nouns are asked, never asserted; scope is inferred from alias interval hits and stated with a one-word override; unresolvable scope checks the broadest interval and marks findings scope-dependent; output that fails the schema is re-asked once, and a second failure ends the run as NO VERDICT (UNKNOWN). Reconciliation with the extraction-cost gate, in writing: the gate governs the LEDGER side — facts enter the ledger only from the per-scene extraction at chekhov commit — while this call types the QUERY side only: it reads no bible text, writes nothing to the ledger, and yields the idea's own tuples for the check; no bible text is ever re-extracted per query.
- Worked trace, end to end, in this plan (Bright-Heart-shaped with Jumper's illustrative names and receipts; the shipped fixture uses real Bright-Heart entries, the mechanism is identical). Raw pasted line, ASR casing: "so tarn is already the marshal in book two when elra first meets him".
- Trace step 1, extraction (the one bounded call): kind idea; scope B2; claims (tarn, title, marshal, B2) and (elra, first_meets, tarn, B2); unknown_nouns none; unknown_predicates none (title is single-valued, first_meets is a declared relation).
- Trace step 2, alias hit (T0, pure): a case-folded trie over alias entries resolves tarn to char.tarn (alias interval [B1.01, B7.end]) and elra to char.elra (the trie also holds Ella and el as ASR variants); marshal is a value, normalised by the pack's value normaliser (case-fold, article-strip) to marshal; the idea tuples are (char.tarn.title, marshal, [B2.01, B2.end]) and (char.elra.first_meets, char.tarn, [B2.01, B2.end]).
- Trace step 3, interval overlap (T0): the entity index for char.tarn.title returns two locked entries — e1 (char.tarn.title, sergeant, [B1.01, B3.03], locked, receipt bible.md#L212 "Tarn serves as sergeant of the river watch until the siege of Harrow") and e2 (char.tarn.title, marshal, [B3.04, B7.end], locked, receipt bible.md#L214 "After the siege the council names Tarn Marshal"); overlap([B2.01, B2.end], e1.t) is true; overlap with e2.t is false.
- Trace step 4, the comparator, named single_value_overlap: conflict(a, b) holds iff a.id = b.id and the predicate's cardinality is single and overlap(a.t, b.t) and norm(a.v) differs from norm(b.v); against e1: marshal differs from sergeant, so CONFLICT; against e2: no overlap, so not tested; a multi-valued predicate never conflicts on value, only against an explicit negation entry.
- Trace step 5, absence queries on the same path (T0): use_before_plant — thread.marshal-title (plant B3.04, due [B3.04, B5.end], pay null) is used at B2.01, and B2.01 precedes B3.04 in reader order, so USE-BEFORE-PLANT; unpaid_due — this idea closes no scope, so nothing fires, and the report's threads-due section lists thread.marshal-title as open regardless; reader order is story order 1..7, the 1,3,2,6,4,5(,7) cascade is written order and never enters the check.
- Trace step 6, verdict text computed by code before any seat is used: INCONSISTENT (T0; time recorded by the fixture, bound under 2 s) · conflicts: char.tarn.title — idea says marshal at B2; locked sergeant [B1.01–B3.03] — bible.md#L212 "Tarn serves as sergeant of the river watch until the siege of Harrow" · absent: thread.marshal-title used at B2, planted B3.04 — bible.md#L214 "After the siege the council names Tarn Marshal" · no-entry: char.elra.first_meets (recorded as candidate, not counted as consistent) · alternatives, each T0-clean before display: (a) move the meeting to B3.05 or later; (b) a decision entry moving the naming to B2 — ripple 2 locked entries and 1 thread, cost_of_change 3, requires a lock event.
- Trace step 7, T1 behind it: the persistent judge session receives the idea, the two cited entries and the thread and returns an evidence table only (entry id, quoted span, supports / conflicts / unaffected / absent) for the semantic residue — here whether "already the marshal" is a title claim or a nickname; every cite is machine-verified before display, code recomputes the verdict, and the fixture stores the raw line, the extraction output, the T0 verdict and the recorded T1 table, with the timing fixture recording T0 under 2 s and the full verdict under 60 s.
- Split path: T0 returns under 2 s with a verdict or NO VERDICT; T1 runs behind it in a persistent judge session (a resumed headless same-family session, no per-idea spawn) and updates the record; the whole verdict lands under 60 s on John's machine with no cross-family seat, and a timing fixture with the real seat is journaled. Verdict honesty: NO VERDICT — UNKNOWN (extraction failed the schema twice, or a T1 cite failed verification) and NO VERDICT — PENDING (judge seat unavailable) are displayed as exactly those words with the reason, are never shown as Consistent, are re-run at the next chekhov invocation, and count in the timing fixture as misses against criterion 2, never as fast passes.
- The T1 judge never emits a verdict word: it returns an evidence table (entry id, quoted span, supports / conflicts / unaffected / absent) and code computes Consistent / Consistent-with-adjustments / Inconsistent by one rule — any conflict with a locked entry gives Inconsistent with alternatives; absences, or conflicts with candidate entries, that a listed ripple pays give Consistent-with-adjustments with the ripple list; Consistent only when every claim is matched to a supporting or unaffected entry; a claim with no entry is listed no-entry and never counts toward Consistent; every cited id and span is machine-verified against ledger and markdown before display, and a failed cite demotes the verdict to NO VERDICT (UNKNOWN) with the failed cite shown; the ripple list is the depends_on closure with lock rungs, a locked entry in the ripple upgrades the ask to 'requires a lock event' priced by ripple count; alternatives on Inconsistent pass T0 before display; every run stamps which model filled the judge seat.
- Verdict records append to the project's own markdown log as project data (PENDING and NO VERDICT entries included, each re-run at the next chekhov invocation until resolved); the log is sample-audited at each lock event (Phase 5), never on a calendar quota; fixture promote turns any verdict into a regression case.
- Criterion-3 fixtures, each labelled real-replay or reconstructed with its source file: six-vs-seven books (T0, fixture #1, real-replay from the frozen pre-decision snapshot); 14 chapters at 6.5-8k vs the 3.5-4.5k rule (T0 word counts); the kishotenketsu leak into Appendix A (T0 doctrine, on the appendix prose); el/Remi/Elra, Raggi/Corvo, Daguan/Durgan (T0 alias intervals, John confirms which drifts were authorial first); 2,500 vs 3,500-word chapters (T0); Anya 13 vs Jess 11 (T0 birth years); Jess's relationship (T1: the recorded judge evidence table is replayed deterministically and the fixture FAILS on any missed cite, exactly as the other T1 fixtures do). Capability split stated per class: T0 catches value conflicts on one id across overlapping intervals, alias-interval misses, word-count and chapter-rule breaches, doctrine terms, birth-year arithmetic and thread absences; T1 is needed only where the drift is a semantic relation with no single-valued predicate — Jess's relationship is the one recorded class of that kind — and it replays from its recorded table with no tolerance.
- Test gating: T0 fixtures are pure and always gate; T1 fixtures replay the recorded seat response by default and fail on any missed cite; --live re-runs the real seat and is the only place an N-of-M tolerance applies, with N, M and the result journaled; the Foreman gate requires T0 plus recorded T1 and never --live.
- Scale debts paid on the real corpus: T0 and full-verdict timing measured on the migrated Bright-Heart and Artificial Magi markdown (the 167k manuscript, the two bibles, the outlines) with the figures in the journal; extraction is batched at commit with an honest backlog count; extraction recall is the criterion-3 corpus itself — an extractor that misses a recorded drift fails that fixture, and the extractor prompt is fixed before any outline.
- STATUS.json is fixed to five fields (project, cascade position, next action, waiting-on-John, last session), enforced by a test, regenerated as a projection from the ledger, the decision record and the verdict log's last entry, never hand-edited, written in the project root. Ecgberht's Strip is per-project strip.json, schema ecgberht-strip-v0 (locked fields phase · active_effort · human_wait · capacity · negative_heartbeat · grasscatch · uncertainty_flags · tool_depth_cell · next_recommended · why_next), append-only with Ecgberht as its single writer, so the skill never writes strip.json: chekhov status pushes the four mapped fields (phase from cascade position; active_effort from project; human_wait from waiting-on-John; next_recommended from next action) through Ecgberht's update heartbeat verb, and the equality test reads strip.json back and asserts those four fields equal STATUS.json's; Stage 2 reads that verb's argument shape before the mapping is fixed; with no Ecgberht present STATUS.json stands alone; Ecgberht ranks across projects and never rewrites the within-project next action.
- chekhov brief <project> is the session-start surface: at most 200 words, line 1 the five status fields, then who is alive, what is locked in scope, threads due, forks open, in reader order; each project CLAUDE.md becomes a one-paragraph consumer telling any host to run it first; chekhov status --line emits the one derived line.
- Session residue has exactly two homes and no third: an unresolved verdict stays in the verdict log as PENDING or NO VERDICT until the next invocation resolves it, and an unanswered or dismissed ask stays in the decision record at rung provisional with its date; anything out of scope is said aloud as a grasscatch line for Ecgberht's catcher and is not stored by the skill.
- From the Phase-2 migration on, the markdown is canonical and the JS bible generators are frozen (kept, not run); existing docx are declared stale until Phase 4's render exists; Word is an output only — any edit John makes in a rendered docx is re-entered in the markdown by hand, and the Phase-4 render hash flags a diverged docx and refuses a clean report until it is re-rendered.
- Submission status per story (drafted / submitted-to / response) is a fact in the story's structural record shown under waiting-on-others in the brief, never a STATUS.json field.

**Deferred (explicitly):**
- An NLI candidate filter and any embedding or retrieval layer beyond entity-indexed interval overlap (research ADOPT 4): revisited only if Phase 2's timing and recall figures show T1 cannot meet 60 s or misses on the corpus.
- The relied lock rung: derived from draft references only at a bible version bump in Phase 5, never per idea (resolves Jumper's a-2 tension by tiering).
- A live voice channel (microphone, tail, stream): v1 intake is paste or file drop, which John already produces from voice-to-text.
- Any prose generation, and docx rendering of any kind: render lands in Phase 4 in the same wave as provenance and the voice guard, behind criterion 1 (the Phase-1 proof is read on LEDGER-REPORT.md, never on a docx).
- A Word-to-markdown round trip (diffing a Word-edited file back into the source): not in v1; markdown is the only editable source.
- A per-session sheet, a settle command and a dismissal tripwire: cut from v1; the verdict log and the decision record hold all residue.
- Word-comment provenance, a GUI or Anchor panel, and full-manuscript LLM consistency re-reads as a primary check (non-goals or rejected).

## Phase 3 — Phase 2 - First real jobs: Bright-Heart decision record and Book-1 cleanliness, AM Spine v4 pass (usage before waves)

Serves criteria 1, 8 and 9 verified on John's screen, and is the doctrine-churn gate in use: the skill refuses to outline until Bright-Heart's doctrine, count, boundary, chapter rule and age category are recorded; the journal entry this phase leaves is the ticket to every later build wave.

**Near-term specifics:**

- The Bright-Heart decision record, delivered as Speaking-Law asks with a recommendation and a computed ripple count each, provisional rung allowed, in this order: (1) whether any Western layer from the 2026 Three-River hybrid stays, with its allow_terms; (2) the doctrine tag kishotenketsu; (3) book count six or seven, with the fork package showing how many threads due in Book 7 fall overdue at Book 6; (4) the Book-1 boundary; (5) the chapter rule (3.5-4.5k vs the 14 chapters at 6.5-8k in Outline v2); (6) the age category (middle grade or young YA), named before any length target.
- Before the Book-1 boundary decision: build the structural record of the existing manuscript (where each ten and ketsu falls, per-chapter word counts), list cut-after-a-triumph candidates, apply the duology kill-gate; if no standalone ending exists at any cut, name the writing job as a beat-level plan the checker will check but not write.
- Cleanliness checklist: Kirk's edit letter and Olivia's structural feedback converted into reader-grounding checklist entries in the decision record, each ticked with a receipt, so the Book-1 pass has a finish line.
- Criterion 1 verified: LEDGER-REPORT.md on John's screen shows zero contradictions with the three named ids T0-verified on prose, the six-book paragraph annotated superseded_by the decision id and listed under the report's superseded heading; the frozen copy in test/fixtures/brightheart-pre-decision/ was taken at the first commit, before ask (3) was answered, so fixture #1 is real-replay (given the private remote confirmed in Phase 0; otherwise it is de-identified and labelled reconstructed).
- The skill drafts journal entry NNNN from the session log for John to sign; his hands-on time is his to budget and is recorded in the entry, not capped by the plan.
- The 30-second test is timed on the five status fields alone and journaled; real sessions run through chekhov brief and their count is recorded in the criterion-8 journal entry (no trial length is fixed by the plan); if John will not move hosts, a thin project-local consumer calls the engine.
- The migration is journaled with the list of files now canonical in markdown; the JS bible generators stay frozen (their retirement is Phase 4's, after John approves a rendered sample per project).
- Second first job: the Artificial Magi Spine v4 package checked against Bible v0.6 through T0 and T1 on the AM markdown (full-text md plus Spine, Outline and Beat md), with the doctrine lint running under AM's Four-Part tag; the AM decision record starts with the doctrine tag and the 2026-07-09 repudiation as allow_terms evidence.
- The Foreman plan encodes the blocker: no Phase 3 or Phase 4 wave until criterion 1 passes on Bright-Heart's real bible AND the journal holds the first-job entry; the build waits for John, and the asks stay at the top of the brief until answered.

**Deferred (explicitly):**

- The trilogy length target: the age category comes first; the 2026 MG/YA length bands remain in VERIFY until a second source is fetched.
- The AM Book-1 lock and its cross-family pass (Phase 5).
- Cowboy Cafe polish, the only first job that exercises prose (Phase 4).
- Rendered docx samples and the generator retirement (Phase 4, with provenance).

## Phase 4 — Phase 3 - Packs and profiles: forms shareable, voices private, one doctrine tag per project

Serves criterion 6 and the structure-creep gate; Gandalf e-3 (form / profile / project separation) was grounded by both refuting families; Decision 1 salvages the four skill-sets as text, not orchestration.

**Near-term specifics:**
- Pack schema (form): beat vocabulary, interval coordinate, structural-record template, checklist, doctrine term list with ordinary-English collisions whitelisted, pick-a-side points. Profile schema (voice): markers, threshold bands, semantic-marker list, private calibration path. Both are NEW files citing the four originals by section; the originals stay untouched.
- Build order: the kishotenketsu pack for Bright-Heart first, defined as a withholding discipline with three pick-a-side points per book (promise contract at the ten; closure at the ketsu with a stated market risk; whether conflict is required at all) stored as per-book decision entries with pack defaults; then the Four-Part pack written in John's own words from his July-2025 lecture notes (Stage 2 reads them before drafting), Savage cited as source, the shareable layer on the publicly documented Weiland and Swain layers, Savage-specific rules kept in the private layer if the notes prove to be class material; then the Eddy pack (Concerto and Symphony map, discourse order plus spiral position as the coordinate); the Prosecution pack in the phase's tail (Opening / Evidence / Closing record; Claim, Ground, Illustrate, Test entries with ground receipts; argument order as the coordinate; the Freedom of Speech draft as its fixture).
- Profiles magi, brightheart and sing live under project data or a private path referenced from the pack, each recording its baseline file list with dates; the Phase-0 privacy test goes live against the pack folders.
- The interval coordinate and the doctrine term lists move out of the Phase-1 hard-code into the packs; one fixture per form proves the ledger core file byte-identical across all four forms; the doctrine-lint precision figure is re-run and journaled.
- Criterion 6 handover test: a fresh seat given only the Eddy pack and a neutral seed produces a structurally correct Concerto and a Symphony outline; the output is scanned for sing-voice terms and must contain zero.
- The divergences among the three voice contracts (magi / brightheart / sing) are surfaced as ONE Speaking-Law ask with a recommendation, never merged silently.
- Second-collection test: two project folders run against one Eddy pack and one sing profile by path reference, so a second collection is a second project with no copied rules.
- Each project carries ONE doctrine tag; the checker refuses the other doctrine's vocabulary unless the project's decision record allow_terms permits it, with the Appendix A leak and the Bright-Heart Western-layer decision as the two live cases.

**Deferred (explicitly):**
- Poetry and political-shorts packs: v2 packs of this same skill, not a second skill.
- A second short-story form beyond the Eddy, and kishotenketsu as a template for any project other than Bright-Heart (PARK, zero spend).
- Sharing with other writers: only the form/profile separation ships in v1; the handover test is the proof, not a release.
- The canonization loop after each book (VERIFY: fetch Writing Excuses 12.30); Phase 5 records promises at outline lock regardless of that verification.

## Phase 5 — Phase 4 - Voice guard, provenance in the rendered docx, render, and restructure-only dictation (the experiment before any prose)

Serves criterion 5 and the voice-homogenisation gate: no generated or restructured prose ships without the guard and provenance in the same slice; mechanics-only lint is refuted by both families, so the guard carries semantic markers and the sit-beside test (research F4: restructure, never regenerate).

**Near-term specifics:**
- Criterion 5 runs as a real experiment BEFORE any prose generation, with its decision rule pre-registered in the journal before any score is computed: the original 'Sing for the Dead' must be classed author and BOTH rewrites (the mechanically flattened one and the sacred-hedged one) must be classed not-author, or the guard fails; two authorial-drift passages from John's own dated drafts (Cowboy Cafe, Viking-Son) must be classed author, so he writes nothing new and drift is not punished; the fixture scorer is the evidenced Voice-Under-Revision 13-marker battery plus authorship-embedding distance to the profile baseline (research F4: a non-fiction harness, no fiction thresholds), and the fixture stores every score beside the pre-registered rule.
- The guard's visible output is an evidence table, never a pass/fail word: per marker, the passage's value against the profile's baseline band with the delta; the sentences that hedge a spiritual event, quoted; and the sit-beside result with its pairs; John overrules any line by hand and the overrule is logged as authorial drift; no model-centroid corpus exists in v1 (one is designed only if the experiment's scores show the band-plus-hedge table cannot separate the three passages).
- Markers: the 13-marker mechanical battery per 100 words (the four the criterion names — em-dash, hyphen-compound, semicolon-list, sentence-length variance — plus contractions, function-word rate, lexical diversity and the rest of the evidenced set) PLUS semantic evidence tasks run at render time only (every sentence hedging a spiritual event with as if / seemed / felt like, quoted; stance shifts; variance against baseline); zero per-idea cost because raw dictation is germline by provenance stamp.
- The sit-beside test is a recorded protocol: N shuffled pairs of author passage vs rewrite, a single-model seat that is given the profile's calibration passages and the two candidates but never the marker list (blind to what the counters measure) picks the author's, accuracy stored in the fixtures; the pre-registered rule above is the acceptance bar for the experiment, and any later operating threshold is stated in the journal after the first run, not hard-coded before it.
- The voice baseline is dated pre-render prose only (the collection, Cowboy Cafe and Viking-Son drafts); the Hubert drafts (2013-14) are excluded or down-weighted so an old voice cannot pull the centroid; the profile records its baseline file list.
- Provenance travels INTO the rendered docx as criterion 5 is locked: every paragraph of a rendered file that contains any generated or restructured prose opens with exactly one of [AUTHOR], [DEVELOPED] or [SUGGESTED], derived from the paragraph's provenance stamp in the markdown (prov author / developed / suggested), never chosen at render time; a file whose every paragraph is prov author renders without tags because the criterion's clause does not apply to it; the test renders a mixed sample and asserts one tag per paragraph in the docx body, each tag equal to its paragraph's stamp, and zero tags in an all-author render; there is no sidecar.
- chekhov render produces docx from markdown carrying those tags and stores a hash of every rendered file; the skill refuses to report a clean ledger while any rendered docx differs from its hash; John approves one rendered sample each for Bright-Heart, Artificial Magi and Cowboy Cafe, and only then are the frozen JS bible generators retired, journaled.
- Dictation-to-prose: prose is produced only from an approved beat, restructured from John's own words (Rambler: gist plus macro operations), born only by an explicit chekhov draft command, never inside chekhov idea, each paragraph stamped prov author (his words unchanged), developed (his words restructured) or suggested (new) — the stamps the render turns into tags; chekhov idea's prose-kind route from Phase 1 (stored as dictated project data, untouched) lands here.
- Live criterion-5 run: Cowboy Cafe polished to submission with the guard watching, journaled, submission status recorded as a structural-record fact; Viking-Son's Symphony restructure is the second prose job, checked against the Eddy pack.

**Deferred (explicitly):**
- A fine-tuned voice model (dropped on cost and lock-in, not on a measured comparison).
- Exemplar-count tuning and continuation-over-instruction (research VERIFY; PARK).
- A tag-free submission copy or Word-comment provenance: not a render option in v1; if John wants either, it is a signed amendment to criterion 5, never a plan choice.
- Generating chapters from a raw ramble in one step (non-goal); fiction operating thresholds are stated after the first run, never before.

## Phase 6 — Phase 5 - Lock events and the Steward commission

Serves criteria 7 and 4 and the per-idea-cost and sycophancy gates: the cross-family pass fires only at book-outline lock, bible version bump, send-to-editor, or on request, and every seat produces evidence rather than a verdict word.

**Near-term specifics:**
- chekhov lock <event> is a gate with a receipt counting findings per seat; a seat returning zero findings is stamped silent, not clean, and the lock does not proceed on silence; a per-seat retry policy; seats resolved from Anchor prefs (review = Grok today; ChatGPT allowed on review seats and stamped model_attested:false); every run stamps which model filled which role.
- The lock input is the ledger DIFF since the last lock tag (a git tag per bible version), so seats review the delta, never the whole bible.
- At book-outline lock the promises the book makes (threads planted here with dues in later books, in reader order) are recorded as thread entries, so the series bible carries reader promises from the moment Book 1 locks.
- A bible version bump derives the relied rung from draft references and re-prices every decision's cost_of_change; a change to a locked decision is itself a lock event with the cross-family pass and a ripple list, so a fifth Bright-Heart restructure is priced, not merely refused.
- First real lock-event pass: the Artificial Magi Spine v4 package before Book-1 lock (the pass the tracker records as not yet run); its live T1 run is the lock-event obligation recorded in the journal.
- Steward integration is STATUS.json plus the update-heartbeat push of Phase 1 and nothing more; the pass-1 HOLD trigger was exercised in this revision: Ecgberht's commission path is COMMISSION_SKILLS in engine/commission.mjs plus a generated commissionable-skills table that admits a skill only with G4 executor-proven evidence and an externally-observable halt class — far more than a table row — so Chekhov is not commissionable in v1 and that path is Grasscatched with this reason.
**Deferred (explicitly):**
- Ecgberht reading the ledger or the verdict log (it receives the four mapped fields through its own heartbeat verb and nothing else); an Anchor panel consuming the status record (later, non-goal in v1).
- The Ecgberht commission path (COMMISSION_SKILLS plus the generated commissionable-skills table with its G4 executor evidence and halt-class requirement): Grasscatched, with the reason, to Ecgberht's own backlog.
- The foundry-level Gandalf elevation-provenance check (the 2026-09-05 live-path drop): a Gandalf ticket for the foundry, not a Chekhov element.
- Submission-platform integration (Duotrope / Submittable) beyond the tracked status fact.
- A second steward, roadmap or campaign memory inside the skill (non-goal); anything beyond the five status fields is Grasscatched to Ecgberht.

## Adversary disputes
- [P5.6] BLOCKER: KEEP → HOLD — Locked criterion 5 requires [AUTHOR]/[DEVELOPED]/[SUGGESTED] provenance into the rendered docx. RC-7: elegance cannot override a locked criterion. RC-6: John must amend criterion 5 or keep tags in the docx.
- [P1.4] MAJOR: KEEP → CUT — Cited need is B-56 (integrated idea 56), a record created in this Stage-1 triage to justify the element — RC-1 fails. The 2026-09-05 live-path drop was a Gandalf elevation lost from a live path, not a missing map row; a row-existence test cannot see that failure (RC-G theater). Foreman already requires per-wave acceptance criteria in the plan; packaging a skill-fixture map beside that transfers nothing.
- [P1.2] MAJOR: KEEP → HOLD — The markdown-source clause is independently ratified; MIGRATION-DEBT.md is not. Grok's 2026-09-05 refutation is this-effort review, not an independent need for a hand-maintained debt file (RC-1 packaging). The file is itself a stale copy and cannot see an unlisted docx (RC-G). Phased migration stays; the debt markdown does not.
- [P1.6] MAJOR: KEEP → HOLD — Shareable-vs-private is user-named, so gitignore plus a pack-folder marker test meet RC-G. The pre-commit check is a git hook, which P1.7 forbids. Compound KEEP smuggles a forbidden hook beside a valid test; packaging transfers nothing.
- [P1.7] MAJOR: KEEP → HOLD — No-hooks extraction is forced by the locked extraction-cost gate. Scheduling the Foreman harness outside John's writing hours has no independent hours record — the same proposer-number class this pass already HOLD'd at P3.6. RC-1 fails for that clause.
- [P2.12] MAJOR: KEEP → HOLD — A project-data verdict log is forced by never-a-second-memory and criterion 2. 'Ten verdicts a week' is a proposer quota with no incident cadence (RC-1) and moves a standing journal burden onto John (RC-4). The sycophancy gate does not specify a weekly sample.
- [P2.13] MAJOR: KEEP → HOLD — The recorded-drift fixtures are criterion 3 and KEEP. Three new-drift fixtures authored by a seat that has not seen the lint are not on that locked list, cite no independent overfitting incident, and are unexercised presumptive capability (RC-1 / RC-2). Blind authorship is this-effort premortem 10, not a user-ratified datum.

The model-centroid corpus generated from the same beats exists only to feed P5.2's unearned DIRECTION output — packaging beside a needed experiment transfers nothing (RC-1), and it precedes the understanding P5.1 is supposed to produce (RC-5).

This KEEP freezes the guard's output shape (toward centroid / toward profile / away from both) before the P5.1 experiment that is supposed to show what the guard can see — RC-5 premature. Cited need is this-effort premortem 5 plus analogical use of the 2026-09-05 mechanical-counter miss, which P5.1 already tests.
- [P6.7] MAJOR: KEEP → CUT — The 2026-09-05 incident is a Gandalf elevation drop. The proposed guard (every Gandalf elevation in an output or kill log) cannot see a Chekhov lock-seat drop (RC-G). === END DRAFT ===

LOOK-IN: you MUST write heartbeat.json as JSON {doing, why, next, load_bearing:true|false, rabbit:false, ts} within the first look-in window. Silence is treated as death — the orchestrator will kill and respawn you. Keep refreshing that file every few actions while you work. RC-6: if this step is not on the critical path to the North Star, STOP, return what you have, set rabbit:true. Elegance: largest result carried by the least machinery. Do not add extra validation nobody asked for. If you notice a rabbit hole, cut it and tidy — pull yourself together. NORTH STAR: One writing skill that keeps ONE checkable ledger per project — the bible's facts with their lock status, the threads planted and paid, the timeline, the structural record in the form's own vocabulary, and the decisions with their cost of change — and checks every dictated idea, scene or change against it in seconds, reserving the cross-family adversarial pass for lock events; it always knows where he is and what comes next, and it renders his words in his own documented voice without normalising it. It is a slice tool the Steward commissions, never a second memory. Forms — the Four-Part conflict spine for Artificial Magi, kishōtenketsu for Bright-Heart, the Eddy (Concerto/Symphony) for the Sing for the Dead stories, the Prosecution for essays — ship as shareable packs, separate from his private voice profiles and his project data; each project carries ONE doctrine tag and the checker refuses the other doctrine's vocabulary unless the project's decision record allows it. New forms (poetry, political shorts) are added later as packs of the same skill, not as a second skill. The bible's source of truth is markdown the skill can check; Word documents are rendered from it. First jobs: Artificial Magi Book 1, a clean Harry-Potter-1-level Bright-Heart Book 1 with its trilogy plan, and the Sing for the Dead collection (every story and novella in it, and a second collection if it comes).

SUCCESS CRITERIA: 1. Bright-Heart's own bible passes the deterministic lint with zero self-contradictions (six-vs-seven books, chapter-length rule, doctrine tag) BEFORE any new outline is produced — verified on the ledger report John opens on his screen. 2. A dictated idea receives a Consistent / Consistent-with-adjustments (ripple list) / Inconsistent (alternatives) verdict that cites ledger entry ids and quoted lines, in under 60 seconds on his machine, with no cross-family seat. 3. Every recorded drift in the two series' histories (six-vs-seven books; 14 chapters at 6.5–8k words vs the 3.5–4.5k rule; the kishōtenketsu leak into Appendix A; el/Remi/Elra, Raggi/Corvo, Daguan/Durgan naming; Jess's relationship; 2,500 vs 3,500-word chapters; Anya 13 vs Jess 11) is caught by the T0 lint or the T1 judge when replayed as a fixture — the regression corpus ships with the skill. 4. "Where am I / what next" for each project comes from ONE status record that the Steward's Strip also reads; the skill and the Steward never disagree. 5. Generated or restructured prose carries [AUTHOR]/[DEVELOPED]/[SUGGESTED] provenance into the rendered docx, and the voice GUARD — mechanical counts PLUS semantic markers (hedging of spiritual events with "as if"/"seemed", stance, sentence-length variance) PLUS the sit-beside model test — separates "Sing for the Dead" from two deliberately normalised rewrites of it: one mechanically flattened, one "sacred-hedged" (session evidence, 2026-09-05: a Gandalf refuter's n=1 experiment showed such a rewrite passes every mechanical counter — a hypothesis this criterion tests, not a settled fact). 6. The Eddy form pack (Concerto + Symphony) can be handed to another writer with no sing-voice rule inside it. 7. The cross-family adversarial pass (Grok / ChatGPT seats from Anchor prefs) fires only at lock events — book outline lock, bible version bump, "send to editor" — or on request; never per idea. 8. The first real job (Bright-Heart decision record + Book-1 cleanliness pass, or the Artificial Magi Spine v4 consistency pass) leaves a journal entry BEFORE any further build wave (usage before waves). 9. THE 30-SECOND TEST on John's screen: from the session-start surface he can name project, cascade position, next action and what is waiting on him within 30 seconds, and it is no more burdensome than "Work on X" is today.
